title: ConcurrentHashMap versus Hashtable
context: How does ConcurrentHashMap differ from Hashtable?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java collections questions (2 of 2)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Hashtable locks the whole table for every operation, so only one thread works at a time. ConcurrentHashMap allows many threads to read without locks and to write to different parts of the table at the same time. Since Java 8 it locks individual bins with synchronized and uses CAS for empty bins. It doesn't allow null keys or values, which avoids ambiguity between a missing key and a null value.

points.title: Fine-grained locking
points.why: Writes lock only one bin, so unrelated keys don't block each other.

points.title: No nulls
points.why: A null value would make get ambiguous, so ConcurrentHashMap rejects nulls.
